verdict: The six rule names and defaults, the config keys, ranges and defaults, the NeoForge file layout, the import order of a Java world (id first, old name last) and the all-or-nothing toggle logic match the Java mod, and each difference I found in the config page and the button is already listed in log/settings.md. What is left is small: a Re-Create world starts ON where Java copies the old world's rules, and a Java world's rules are imported once only, so later changes made in the Java mod are ignored.

findings.what: Re-Create of a world (the world list has it, title/create_world.rs `of_world`) opens the Create New World screen, and `track_screen` sets the choice to ON and writes `true`. Java builds the button from the rules of the screen (`isBalancedHardcoreEnabled(uiState.getGameRules())`), and vanilla copies the old world's rules into that screen, so the Java button shows the old world's BMH state. A world whose BMH rules were OFF is re-created with every rule ON. The coordinator's note in the log asked the parity review to look at this; the Differences list does not name it.

evidence.ours: horizon/native/mixins/bmh/bmh_settings.rs:300-301 `*lock(&CLIENT_CHOICE) = Some(true);` and `game.native_set_setting(crate::game::bmh::ID, logic::CHOICE_SETTING, logic::bool_text(true));` (run for every Create screen that follows another screen, with no check for a re-created world)
evidence.host: crates/horizon-client/src/title/create_world.rs:70-76 `pub(super) fn of_world(level: &crate::save::Level, commands: bool, dir: &std::path::Path)` and `let (pack_dir, data_packs) = crate::datapack::for_recreate(dir);` (Horizon has Re-Create and builds the screen from the old world's directory)

findings.fix: When the title opened the screen with `of_world` (Re-Create), start the choice from the old world's `<world>/bmh/rules.txt` (any rule on gives ON, as Java `anyMatch`), or add the case to Differences and GAPS S2. Check first that the Re-Create screen has the id `world_create`.

findings.what: The rules of a Java world are imported once, at the first open (when `rules.txt` does not exist). After that the file wins. Java reads the game rules saved data at every load, so a world that goes back to the Java mod, has `/gamerule bmh:... false` run there, and returns to Horizon keeps the old Horizon values. The log says 'After that the file is the truth' but lists it neither under 'Could not' nor in Differences, and GAPS S1 does not allow it.

evidence.ours: horizon/native/mixins/bmh/bmh_settings.rs:255-256 `let file = std::fs::read_to_string(rules_path(&dir)).ok().map(|text| logic::parse_rules(&text)); let first_open = file.is_none();` and logic/src/settings.rs:171-173 `if let Some(rules) = file { return rules; }`
evidence.java: common/src/main/java/github/mrornithorynque/bmh/mixin/N_SavedDataGameRulesMixin.java:28 `BMHGameRules.migrateLegacyNames(cir.getReturnValue());` (runs on every read of the saved data, and the game rules are the saved data)

findings.fix: Add a line to Differences ('a world shared between the Java mod and Horizon: the first Horizon open decides'). If shared worlds matter, compare the modification time of `game_rules.dat` with `rules.txt` at each open.
